messages.subject: Fwd: more questions about CODEX
parts:
Begin forwarded message:

Date: February 24, 2015 at 10:44:04 AM EST
From: Herenger yvan <yvanhe...@yahoo.fr>
Subject: more questions about CODEX
To: Yuchao Jiang <yuc...@mail.med.upenn.edu>, NancyZhang <n...@wharton.upenn.edu>

Hello,

I am still working on your package, and I have a new question/suggestion for you and the online user group. My first steps were to test the CODEX package on our server with your toy data package WES.1KG.WUGSC (I did without any problem) and then with our data sample (we succeed in doing this thanks to your advice).

Now my deal is to test the whole data from our targeted exome experiment, and I met a problem : our targeted exom encompasses 36 genes on about 17 chromosomes I think, and the BED file doesn't suit the first steps of the CODEX workflow :
In the demo :
chr <- 22
I tried :
chr <- c("chr1", "chr2", "chr3", "chr4", "chr5", "chr6", "chr7", "chr8", "chr9", "chr10", "chr11", "chr12", "chr13", "chr14", "chr15", "chr16", "chr17", "chr18", "chr19", "chr20", "chr21", "chr22")
But after it doesn't succeed in the step
exomtarg <- exomtarg[exomtarg[, 1] == chr, ]
In the getbambed function. And even if I remove this step, although I can succeed in the getbambed function, I cannot succeed in the getcoverage function.

The other problem I met in the getcoverage function is the following : I removed the "> exomtarg <- exomtarg[exomtarg[, 1] == chr, ]" step in the getbambed function and went on with my data, but I couldn't go further than the "> which <- RangesList(quack = IRanges(st - 10000, ed + 10000)) in the getcoverage function, because of the ranges values between the "> st <- start(ref)[1]" and the "> ed <- end(ref)[length(ref)]", the ed being unluckily smaller than ths st because of the targeted exome experiment design. So, I sorted the bed file from the smaller range to the bigger and tried again but finally the message I get when I am at the getcoverage step is :
Erreur dans names(x@listData) <- value :
 attribut 'names' [22] doit être de même longueur que le vecteur [1]

I join you in this mail the first unsorted_bedFile and the sorted_bedFile, so that you can have an idea of the problem.

What do you think about it ?
Is CODEX usable with targeted exome data ?
Is it possible to use a bef file with mutiple gene targets on several chromosomes, and can we give to the 'chr' value different chrosomomes possibilities ?

This kind of experiment design (targeted exomes) is still very frequent in France, and it would be great to use CODEX that way. If not, I think we can use CODEX with our data chromosome after chromosome : it should work very well that way.

Thank you again for your advices and your answers !

Kindly yours,

Yvan

messages.author: 94ec915e8ce36448
messages.subject: Re: more questions about CODEX
parts:
Hello Yvan,

Yes, you are correct. CODEX is originally designed for whole exome sequencing and not specifically for exon targeted sequencing. It analyzes each chromosome separately as do many other softwares. We do, however, have collaborations at UPENN where we adapt CODEX to call CNVs from targeted next-gen sequencing data. In this sense, we pulled the read depth across all chromosomes and normalize the genome-wide read depth matrix all at once.

I will try to come up with a version for exon targeted sequencing but essentially the code would look like getting coverage, gc content, mappability for targets on each chromosome, combine them together as one matrix (read depth) and vector (GC content, mappability) for the entire genome, and then run the QC, and normalization. For targeted sequencing, since there aren't too many targets in each gene, we use thresholding rather than CBS for CNV calling. Namely, take the log ratio of Y_qc divided by Yhat[[optK]] with optK being the optimal value of the number of latent factors.

For your question on the bed file, again, the error is due to the fact that CODEX doesn't work in a cross-chromosome fashion at this moment. However, for each chromosome--you are right--the bed file needs to be sorted with positions of targets in rising orders.

Thank you for all of your questions and suggestions--they certainly help us improve our software and understand the problem better. However, for your future contacts, could you email to the user group directly at codex_...@googlegroups.com (and cc me and Nancy if you wish)? This way, more users can see the questions and solutions.

I will keep you posted on the version of CODEX for targeted sequencing.

Cheers,
Yuchao
